guide.summary: Joseon palaces, national and city museums, parks and an aquarium, with hotel dining rooms, a gomtang house, cocktail lounges, a hotel bakery and coffee bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan museum days around closures: Seoul Museum of Art closes every Monday, Seodaemun Prison History Hall closes Mondays and moves to winter hours of 09:30–17:00 from November, and the National Palace Museum of Korea closes on the last Monday of each month.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Seoul Museum of Art (Seosomun) and Seodaemun Prison History Hall close every Monday, while the National Palace Museum of Korea closes on the last Monday of the month.

toolkit.label: Late openings
toolkit.copy: The National Museum of Korea and MMCA Seoul both stay open until 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays. The National Palace Museum of Korea runs to 21:00 on Saturdays, and the Seoul Museum of Craft Art opens until 21:00 on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Fridays to Sundays through 30 November.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: La Yeon and Continental at The Shilla Seoul take a KRW 50,000 per person deposit, with Continental bookings opening on the first day of the month two months ahead. SEA LIFE COEX Aquarium sells tickets online and says online buyers can skip the queue.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: La Yeon and Continental recommend smart casual dress and limit the main dining hall to guests aged 6 and above. 1914 Lounge & Bar at Josun Palace has a casual dress code, turns away training pants, pajamas, bathrobes and slippers, and takes bar orders only from 18:00.

guide.dek: Check each palace's notice board before you go, because access to parts of Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung and Deoksugung is restricted this autumn.
intro: Seoul's royal palaces are the obvious place to start: Gyeongbokgung on Sajik-ro, Changdeokgung on Yulgok-ro and Deoksugung on Sejong-daero. Each palace posts notices of works and restricted areas on its own site, so check them before you go. This autumn, fire-suppression works limit access to Changdeokgung's government offices area, and outer wall works at Deoksugung run to 19 November. Gyeongbokgung is also running a royal culture academy at Heungbokjeon. Next to Gyeongbokgung, the National Palace Museum of Korea opens until 21:00 on Saturdays and closes on the last Monday of each month.

Several of the city's major museums stay open late, so you can spend a day at the palaces and see art in the evening. The National Museum of Korea opens until 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and its special exhibition "Tour of National Treasures" runs until 29 November. MMCA Seoul, on Samcheong-ro, keeps the same late nights and is showing Do Ho Suh until 9 February 2027 and the Korea Artist Prize 2026 until 6 December. At Leeum Museum of Art in Hannam, Koo Jeong A's exhibition runs until 27 December.

For a quieter or more unusual day, you can visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall, which closes on Mondays and switches to 09:30–17:00 hours from November. The Seoul Museum of Craft Art near Anguk opens until 21:00 on most evenings through 30 November, with Equinox running until March 2027. If you are travelling with children, Seoul Children's Grand Park is open from 05:00 to 22:00 every day, and its autumn festival runs until 7 November, although its botanical garden is closed until the second half of 2027.

For dining, The Shilla Seoul puts several options under one roof. The Parkview serves breakfast from 06:00, La Yeon on the 23rd floor serves Korean cuisine at lunch and dinner, and Pastry Boutique is open from 07:00 to 22:00. Hadongkwan's Myeongdong branch serves gomtang from 07:00 to 16:00 and closes on Sundays. For coffee, you can visit Fritz Coffee in Dohwa or Wonseo. For drinks, try The Library at The Shilla or 1914 Lounge & Bar on the 24th floor of Josun Palace.
summaryCards: Pair Gyeongbokgung with the National Palace Museum of Korea next door, but check the palace notices for areas closed this autumn.
Start with breakfast at The Parkview from 06:00 or coffee at Fritz Coffee (Wonseo), which opens daily at 09:00.
La Yeon and Continental at The Shilla Seoul take a KRW 50,000 per person deposit and admit only guests aged 6 and above to the main dining hall.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Palace opening hours for Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung and Deoksugung were not on the pages read, and neither were regular hours for Leeum Museum of Art or Seoul Arts Center; SEA LIFE COEX Aquarium showed only a same-day snapshot. Jungsik, Hadongkwan, 1914 Lounge & Bar and both Fritz Coffee branches publish addresses and hours or booking links but no dated 2026 content, so they are rated medium. Many input places could not be confirmed: Gwangjang Market, Tosokchon and Myeongdong Kyoja had certificate errors; Charles H and Anthracite returned 403; London Bagel Museum's domain did not resolve; Mingles and Lotte World returned no readable content; N Seoul Tower's pages had an encoding error; Bar Cham and Center Coffee have no official websites; and Alice Cheongdam, Maison M.O and Breadypost could not be identified. Coverage of bakeries and cocktail bars therefore relies on hotel venues.
